_comment: What the featured years (1971, 1985, 1997, 2008, 2022) say outside the event list: the portals' summaries, policies and people (content/history.json), the portal scenes (src/data/portals.ts) and the guide's openings (src/guide/guide-scripts.ts). `text` is the wording as reviewed: tests fail when the app's text changes without a new review. `evidence`: quotes from content/sources.json (checked by scripts/review_featured.py), rate figures recomputed from H.10 (scripts/check_rates.py), and the office checks of scripts/build_media.py. Events have their own evidence in content/annual-events.json.

items.text: In August 1971 the United States suspended the convertibility of the dollar into gold, so other governments could no longer exchange their dollars for gold. By 1973 fixed exchange rates had given way to floating ones: the yen went from about 357 to about 280 per dollar.

items.text: 1971. For more than twenty years, most major currencies have been fixed to the dollar, and the dollar to gold. This is the year that system breaks.

items.note: 'Most major currencies': Canada's dollar floated from 1950 to 1962 and again from 1970 (see the 1950 and 1970 events).

items.text: In September and October 2008 a financial crisis that began in the United States spread around the world. Between late June and late November the won fell from about 1,040 to about 1,470 per dollar, and the Australian dollar lost about a third of its value against the dollar.
